name: OpenEXR (Python bindings and tools)
role: Reference EXR library: write and read float multi-channel EXR from Python; header and check CLIs
summary: The reference OpenEXR implementation. The PyPI `OpenEXR` wheel reads and writes scanline, tiled and deep EXR from Python with numpy arrays, with named channels, per-file compression (ZIP, PIZ, DWAA, B44 and others) and header attributes. The native package also ships exrheader, exrcheck, exrinfo and exrmetrics.
use_when: Write or inspect float or half EXR (render passes, depth, masks) from a Python script with exact pixel control
Check what compression, channels and data window an EXR carries before a delivery step
avoid_when: Colour conversion, resize or compositing of EXR: openimageio-oiiotool

install.macos: python3 -m venv output/venv && output/venv/bin/pip install OpenEXR==3.5.5 numpy

notes: 2026-11-27: the lead said Homebrew 3.5.4 and the tools alone; PyPI has OpenEXR 3.5.5 (uploaded 2026-11-23, Python >=3.11, BSD-3-Clause in the wheel metadata). The wheel has the Python module only, no exr* command-line tools.
2026-11-27: File.channels() groups R, G, B, A into one RGBA array and fails if they differ in pixel type (use separate_channels=True); File.header() must be copied before the file closes.

assessment.rationale: PyPI 3.5.5 uploaded 2026-11-23; repository pushed 2026-11-17. It is the reference EXR implementation and the only catalogued route to exact float channel writes from code; oiiotool converts and composites but does not expose the library's header and compression control directly. The exr* CLIs (exrcheck, exrmetrics) were not exercised.

evidence.result: 17 checks pass, repeat processes identical: float32 RGBA plus a depth.Z channel round-trip bit-exact with ZIP, PIZ and no compression; header compression matches; values up to 37.97 kept; half RGBA matches a float16 cast; a non-EXR file is rejected. Python 3.12.2, numpy 2.5.5.
evidence.scope: Python wheel round trip of scanline files on 32x24 random data; not exrcheck/exrmetrics, tiled, deep or multipart files, lossy DWA/B44, or interop with other readers; macOS arm64.
